abstract: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) requires coordinated management of scarce human brain tissue resources, standardized metadata, and transparent tracking of tissue-to-data transformations across distributed laboratories and centers. We present the Neuroanatomy-Anchored Information Management Platform (NIMP), a consortium-scale web-based application system developed to coordinate multimodal single-cell omics resource generation and maintain end-to-end provenance throughout the tissue-to-bytes life cycle. NIMP integrates donor registration, anatomical annotation, tissue allocation, sequencing workflows, quality assurance and quality control, and archive-data deposition within a unified data ecosystem infrastructure. Over 3 years of production-strength deployment, the platform has managed BICAN consortium's data and metadata for 762 human donors, 8,449 brain slabs, and 21,781 sequencing libraries across 11 laboratories, collectively supporting generation of more than 18 million single cells. NIMP provides a scalable and reusable platform for provenance-aware resource management, FAIR data generation, and future large-scale atlas and multi-network data coordination initiatives.
